environment.note: This checks which navigation events each engine fires and what each history API can read — deterministic pass/fail observations, not a timing benchmark. CPU/GPU/RAM do not affect the result, so they are intentionally omitted. The probe stands up two throwaway localhost origins (127.0.0.1 vs localhost on different ports = genuinely different origins) so cross-origin behavior is real, not simulated.

subject.name: Navigation API (window.navigation)
subject.install: python -m playwright install chromium firefox webkit
subject.note: All three engine builds are the ones bundled with the pinned Playwright version below.

baseline.name: History API (history.pushState / popstate / hashchange)
baseline.note: The Navigation API is compared against the History API it aims to replace. Both are exercised in the same page against the same 11 triggers; the comparison is by observed behavior, not by measured timing.

cross_browser.webkit: Measured firsthand (Playwright WebKit 26.4) — but Playwright's WebKit is NOT Safari. window.navigation is absent in this build, whereas caniuse lists Safari 26.2+ as supporting it. We did NOT measure real Safari. The post and results.json flag this split explicitly: the WebKit result is a real observation about the Playwright E2E environment, not a claim about Safari.
cross_browser.safari: NOT measured. Safari 26.2+ support is cited from caniuse, never presented as firsthand.

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: none discarded — all evidence for this run is small and committed
raw_artifacts.note: This run produces no large raw artifacts. The deterministic evidence — probe-result.json (per-engine surface + trigger observation matrix + history stack readout + spa intercept result) and router-check.json (npm dist grep of shipped routers) — is committed. The npm packages pulled for the router grep are throwaway and not committed.
